discoveries.discovery_sentence: State Bank of India recorded a -0.45 percentage point change in deposits as a share of deposits plus borrowings from March 2026 to June 2026 on a standalone basis.

why_it_matters.text: Growth in the deposit balance does not necessarily raise deposits’ share of this funding denominator when reported borrowings also expand.
The history uses the issuer’s SBI SOLO columns. SBI GROUP columns and net advances are kept separate rather than substituted into the standalone funding ratio.
The eight observed quarter ends provide a funding-mix history; they do not by themselves identify the economic cause or the true onset of a funding change.

counterargument.statement: Borrowings can support balance-sheet deployment and financing choices rather than indicate a deposit shortage. Other liabilities, currency composition, liquidity buffers and lending quality are outside this accounting denominator.

SBI Gram Seva : Rural Development
• Inaugurated the SBI Gram Seva program in Jhunjhunu District,
Rajasthan. The project is being implemented by Arpan Seva Sanstha
for integrated rural development.
• SBI Gram Seva program was launched in Kondagaon District,
Chhattisgarh, implemented by Samarthan – Centre for Development
Support for integrated rural development.
• Gram Seva launched the SBI Sammaan – Hom(e)age to the National
Heroes project at Rudha village, Sitapur District, Uttar Pradesh,
implemented by Sahbhagi Sikshan Kendra in tribute to Param Vir
Chakra Awardee Shaheed Captain Manoj Kumar Pandey.
• Applications for the YFI 2025–26 batch opened on February 11, 2025,
receiving 3,36,864 registrations and 76,317 applications. Following
interviews across six cities, 161 Fellowships were offered, and 68
Fellows joined the batch during the Orientation Programme held at
Barefoot College–SWRC, Tilonia, Rajasthan.
SBI Youth for India Fellowship Program
• The foundation stone for the SBIF Sashakti: Construction of Girls’
Hostel Complex was laid, in partnership with Akhand Jyoti Eye Hospital
and YSSACT. The initiative aims to empower rural girls in Saran, Bihar,
through safe residential facilities and quality education in optometry and
allied fields.
SBIF Sashakti
• SBI Foundation, in partnership with Dr. Reddy’s Foundation, launched
the Swavlamban – Grow PwD Centre at Mysore to empower 1,330
Persons with Disabilities across five centres—Agra, Dehradun, Mysore,
Pune, and Jabalpur—through employability training, career readiness
modules, and sustainable livelihood opportunities over two years.
• SBIF CoE: Samagra Shiksha project launched at Narmadapuram,
Madhya Pradesh, in partnership with CBM India Trust. The three-year
initiative supports 200 Children with Disabilities through education and
therapeutic interventions.
• SBIF CoE: Samarthya project launched at Pimpri-Chinchwad in
partnership with Vipla Foundation. The three-year initiative supports
early identification and therapy for children with hearing impairment,
providing 1,250 hearing aids through the Dhvani Early Intervention
Centre.

SBIF LEAP : Livelihoods
• The SBIF LEAP–I-CUBE project, in collaboration with NSRCEL,
organised a webinar, titled “What Do Donors Expect from Incubation
Programmes”, engaging 99 participants, including incubation managers,
entrepreneurs, and stakeholders to facilitate exchange of best practices
and insights to strengthen donor-supported incubation models.
• SBIF LEAP – Skilling for Future, launched with SRF Foundation at
Mysore Skill Centre, to upskill 3,000 youth in IT and Green Jobs,
enabling participants with market-oriented skills for sustainable careers.
• SBIF LEAP – Ma Ki Roti was launched, in Mahasamund, Chhattisgarh,
in partnership with Maa Foundation to promotes women’s
entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihoods by empowering SHG
women to operate 15 community canteens across Odisha, Chhattisgarh
and Meghalaya.
SBIF ILM : Education
• The Foundation Stone Laying Ceremony for the Tribal Girls’ Hostel at
Niwali Village, Barwani District, Madhya Pradesh, was held in
collaboration with AIDENT Social Welfare Organisation (ASWO) and
Kasturba Gandhi National Memorial Trust (KGNMT). The project aims
to provide safe and modern accommodation for 220 tribal girls,
supporting their access to education in a secure environment.
• On September 12, 2025, the Boccia Sports Federation of India (BSFI)
organised a Boccia Awareness Programme with over 70 participants.

• Shri C S Setty, Chairman of SBI, inaugurated the SBI ARISA (AI,
Robotics and IoT for Smart Agriculture) Lab at PJTSAU Campus,
Hyderabad on 19th December 2025. The event was attended by
officials from Hyderabad Circle, PJTSAU, SBI Foundation, and AgHub
Foundation. The lab serves as a one-stop centre for training, research,
and development in smart agriculture.
• Shri Ashwini Kumar Tewari, MD (CB&S), SBI, launched the Gram
Seva project with Aroh Foundation on 26 December 2025 in Hardoi
District, Uttar Pradesh.
• ‘SBI Sammaan – Hom(e)age to the National Heroes’ project was
honoured with the Social and Business Enterprise Responsible
Award 2025, held at New Delhi on 12 December 2025.
• The SBI YFI 2024-25 Batch Valediction was held from 1–5 November
2025 at State Bank Academy, Gurugram.
• Shri Nitin Gadkari (Minister for Road Transport & Highways, GoI),
Shri Chandrashekhar Bawankule (Revenue Minister, GoM &
Guardian Minister, Nagpur), and Shri Sanjay Prakash (MD & CEO, SBI
Foundation) inaugurated SBIF Jivanam on 2 November 2025,
supporting 100 pediatric heart surgeries with Swami Vivekanand
Medical Mission (SVMM) Hospital, Nagpur.
• SBIF Garima, providing shelter for 40 elderly women by Vasavya
Mahila Mandali, was inaugurated on 28 October 2025. The project
creates dignified living spaces for elderly women through SBI
Foundation’s CSR initiatives.
• SBIF Cancer Care, partnered with Dr. Sheela Sharma Memorial
Charitable Trust, Mathura, was inaugurated on 28 December 2025.
Guests of Honour Dr. G. K. Rath (Former Director, NCI AIIMS Jhajjar),
Dr. Neerja Bhatla (Padma Shri, Former Prof. O&G AIIMS), Dr. N. C.
Prajapati (Former DG Medical Education, UP) attended. The project
screens 1 lakh for breast, cervical, oral cancers, vaccinates 1,400–
1,500 for HPV, and provides free treatment.
• SBI Foundation’s Sashakti team won the SABERA Awards 2025 on
12 December for SBIF–Sashakti, providing legal awareness and
assistance to underprivileged women and victims of sexual/gender￾based violence in New Delhi urban slums.
• SBI Foundation won the India Childcare Champion Award 2025 in
the CSR category from FORCES for early childhood care
contributions.
• SBIF LEAP: SMART-CROP was inaugurated on 29 October 2025 in
Hyderabad with UAS Raichur. The project empowers 8,200
smallholder farmers in Karnataka/Telangana using AI/ML, satellite
imaging, and remote sensing for real-time crop monitoring.
• Sugamya Bharat App launched on 10 October 2025 at Purple Fest
2025, Goa, under SBIF CoE: Samarthya – Sugamya Bharat with NAB
Delhi and DEPwD. The accessible app offers government services,
welfare schemes, jobs, assistive tech, and other assistance to 1 lakh+
Persons with Disabilities.
• Inclusive Action Centre (IAC) under SBIF CoE Samagra Shiksha:
Action for Inclusive Education was inaugurated on 12 November 2025
at Niphad, Nashik, Maharashtra, by Pratham Mumbai Education
Initiative. The 3-year initiative (July 2024–June 2027) supports 250
children with disabilities, engages 1,000 peers, and reaches 3,000
community members for inclusive education.
• Hon’ble Mohan Yadav, CM Madhya Pradesh, and Smt. Pratima
Bagri, Minister of State, felicitated Panna City under Swachh
Survekshan 2024-25 on 14 October 2025 for SBIF CONSERW: Waste
No More. The project, Implemented by SBI
Foundation, in association with PMC (Panna Municipal Corporation)
and SAAHAS improved the city's national ranking from 750 (FY23-24)
to 62 (FY24-25).
• Hon’ble Shri Rajnath Singh, Defence Minister, conferred the
Raksha Mantri Award 2025 for “Swachha Chaavni – Swastha
Chaavni” to Varanasi Cantonment Board (VCB) on 16 December
2025 for SBIF CONSERW: Waste No More project, implemented with
Chintan Foundation, VCB.

Economy in Sweet Spot 
• Global growth remains resilient, with easing inflationary pressures despite
exacerbating geopolitical & extreme weather event risks. The Apr’24 IMF WEO report
raises global growth forecast for 2024 to 3.2%, 10 bps higher than its Jan’24 update

growth to 6.8% in FY25 from 6.5% in Jan’24 update and 6.3% in Oct’23 update (NSO
estimates @ 7.6% in FY24)
• In FY24, credit offtake recorded growth of 20.2% while deposits grew by 13.5% and
the momentum with some moderation, is expected to continue in FY25 too
• Domestic financial sector remains largely insulated from the global uncertainties,
driven by an intrinsic resilience through confluence of regulatory forbearance and
policy imperatives
